route: /style-board/ (the style board: module table:grid, longest and shortest copy, photos as grey frames; no competitor section shows this module)

findings.issue: Still open after two reviews: at 390 px the four-column size table still runs past the right edge. The Weight column shows only 'We' and '12 / kg' clipped at the screen edge, and a faint shade is the only sign the table scrolls. Meanwhile the short cells wrap word by word ('About / 2 / years', 'Size / option'), so every row is three lines tall.
findings.reference: On the competitor's phone pages nothing is clipped at the edge; their facts read in full at the content width.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 600px): set .block--table .table-block :is(th, td) { padding-inline: 0.5rem } with :first-child { padding-inline-start: 0 }, and set white-space: nowrap on the short cells (td:not(:last-child), thead th). The four short columns then fit about 350 px and the last one wraps. If they still overflow, make the right-edge fade on .table-block__scroll[data-scroll="sideways"] wider and darker so the cut-off reads as a sideways scroll.

findings.issue: Still open: at 390 px the label column ('Detail') still takes about 40% of the table. That squeezes the spec column to about 20 characters a line, so rows run 6 to 15 lines ('Humid storage', 'Adhesive compatibility') and the 315-word table becomes a narrow strip about 1,900 px tall with empty space under every label.
findings.reference: The competitor's phone text runs the full content width at about 35–45 characters a line; it never packs prose into a column this narrow.
findings.fix: In reference.css, inside @media (max-width: 600px), stack the two-column table: .block--table .table-block:not(:has(thead tr > :nth-child(3))) tr { display: block; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--border-table) } and its th, td { display: block; border: 0; padding-inline: 0 }. Make the first cell a bold label over a full-width text cell, and hide the thead visually. Keep the four-column m5 table as a table.

findings.issue: Still open: the 'Specification and consequence' column still runs about 100–115 characters a line ('Made from 90% recycled materials and available in 3 shapes: thong, standard bikini and full coverage. The water-'). The table still spans the whole content width of about 1,130 px, so .block--table .table-block__scroll { max-width: calc(70ch + 20rem) } is not taking effect.
findings.reference: The competitor keeps body text to a short measure of about 60–75 characters a line.
findings.fix: Check that the max-width actually reaches the wrapper that sets the table's width; the table itself may be the element at width: 100% of the section. If it doesn't, cap the cells directly: .block--table .table-block table { inline-size: auto; max-inline-size: 100% } and .block--table .table-block td:last-child { max-inline-size: 70ch }. The text column then keeps about 70 characters beside the label column, starting at the heading's left edge.

findings.issue: Still open: the m5 heading ('Toddler Sizes and Custom Size Runs') is still set in a regular weight, while m9's table heading on the same board is bold DM Sans 700. Two headings of the same level show different weights, at 390 px as well.
findings.reference: The competitor sets every section h2 in one heavy weight throughout.
findings.fix: Set font-weight: 700 on .block--table h2 (the table block's heading, in every variant) to match the site's h2 weight, and leave its fitted size alone.

findings.issue: At 390 px the first cell of each row (and the header) is inset about 16 px from the content's left edge, so the labels 'Detail', 'Kraft paper' and 'Size option' start to the right of the heading and intro above them. Their row rules still start at the edge (m5 too).
findings.reference: The competitor starts its section text and facts on one left edge.
